notes: §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR5 at --std 85, with 'file' the physical file (§1985:II.2): a re-OPEN of an open file-name answers 41 through FileRegistry.RefusedAsAlreadyOpen, and the OPEN of a physical file another file-name of the run unit holds open answers 41 through FileRegistry.SharedOpenAttempt (kb/Work PB6161, the owner's decision of 2026-11-24); each succeeds after the holder's CLOSE. Witnesses g85_f19_01 and pb6161_second_select_opens_an_open_file_85. Decided on PB6161's branch by a reader (CONFORMS) and a refuter (UPHELD) at commit 8bdbd239ac: at --std 85 every OPEN of a physical file the run unit holds open answers 41 and leaves the file unaffected, in every mode, through the same file-name, another SELECT, another spelling of the ASSIGN path (one host file identity, PhysicalFileTable.For), a second name in one OPEN statement, a called program or an EXTERNAL file; 00 after a plain CLOSE or a CANCEL; 41 after CLOSE REEL or UNIT; 38 through any name after CLOSE WITH LOCK.

next.reason: 1985 GR5: each subsequent OPEN of 'that same file' must follow a CLOSE, and 'file' is 'the physical file regardless of the file-name used in the COBOL program' (§1985:II.2), so the OPEN of a physical file another file-name of the run unit holds open is status 41, 'An OPEN statement is attempted for a file in the open mode' (§1985:VII.1.3.5). 2023 keys 41 to the file connector (§2023:14.9.27.4 GR2 'The file connector referenced by file-name-1 shall not be open'; §2023:9.1.13.7 GR1 'attempted for a file connector in an open mode') and arbitrates another connector's OPEN by the sharing facility (§2023:9.1.15, Table 19; 00 or 61). The re-OPEN of one file-name behaves the same in both editions; the OPEN through a second file-name does not (kb/Work PB6161, PB6165).
